entities.summary:
James Barnor Hon. FRPS, OV is a Ghanaian photographer who has been based in London since the 1990s. His career spans six decades, and although for much of that period his work was not widely known, it has latterly been discovered by new audiences. In his street and studio photography, Barnor represents societies in transition in the 1950s and 1960s: Ghana moving toward independence, and London becoming a multicultural metropolis.

He has said: "I was lucky to be alive when things were happening..when Ghana was going to be independent and Ghana became independent, and when I came to England the Beatles were around. James Barnor was a painters & sculptors from Accra (b. 1929-06-06, Accra). A moderately significant entity in the historical record. Relevant to cause-and-effect analysis.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: James Barnor's street and studio photography provides a unique perspective on Ghana's transition to independence and London's multiculturalization in the 1950s and 1960s. His work has been rediscovered, offering insights into these pivotal moments.
